question.worked_solution:
The variable $x$ is being *multiplied* by $-8.$ To isolate $x$, we can perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-8.$ So, we divide both sides of the equation by $-8.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-8x & =-56 \\ \frac{-8x}{-8} & =\frac{-56}{-8} \\ \frac{-8x}{-8} & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-8$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-8x}{-8} & =7 \\ \frac{\cancel{-8}x}{\cancel{-8}} & =7 \\ x & =7\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
